units.function: Unit tests for role-derived Agent permission defaults, normalization of stored overrides and create-versus-patch schema semantics for Agent and Skill creation authority.
units.dependencyDirection: Shared request/storage schemas and AgentPermissionsService normalize a small permission object from Agent role plus explicit stored fields before routes and access checks consume it.
units.keyDataModels: Agent role, canCreateAgents, canCreateSkills, canAssignTasks, full permissions schema and partial update schema.
units.lifecycle: Only the exact CEO role receives Agent-creation permission by default; explicit overrides win. Every role receives Skill-creation permission by default, including legacy records that omit the field. Full parsing defaults omission to true, while patch parsing preserves omission as unchanged and explicit false remains false.
units.testAssessment: Five concise cases pin intended defaults, override preservation and correct tri-state patch behavior. Missing are unknown/Unicode/case-normalized roles beyond examples, migration impact counts, policy versioning, permission provenance/expiry, deny conditions, separation of duties, Skill risk classes, organization scope and end-to-end enforcement. Tests intentionally prove a broad default rather than least privilege.
units.designRationale: Keep Agent hiring narrowly held while making Skill authoring broadly available and preserving backward compatibility for records created before the Skill permission field existed.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must distinguish harmless reusable prompts from executable/tool-bearing Skills and ensure an Agent cannot expand its or peers' effective capabilities through a permissive content-creation default.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT the default-on canCreateSkills rule and role-name-as-authority model. Default all effectful capability creation to deny; use explicit versioned grants scoped by tenant/project, Skill risk class, tool/data permissions, expiry and accountable grantor. Preserve the useful omitted-versus-explicit-false patch semantics and run a deliberate migration rather than silently elevating legacy records.
units.responsibilityConflict: Every role, including ordinary Agents, can create a Skill by omission, which may become a durable instruction/tool supply-chain artifact without accountable approval. Role strings and booleans do not identify who granted authority, for what purpose, over which data/tools or under which responsibility contract.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres end-to-end tests for run-bound Agent Secret metadata/value access, binding resolution, success auditing, runtime log-redaction registration and denial of low-trust/special-scope callers.
units.dependencyDirection: An Agent actor and heartbeat run enter Secret routes; SecretService resolves Agent and run-snapshotted Project bindings, decrypts a local-encrypted version, registers the returned value with the run redaction registry, writes SecretAccessEvent/ActivityLog records and returns metadata or plaintext value.
units.keyDataModels: Company Secret/provider/version, target binding/config path/projection class, Agent/run/key scope, run context manifest and redaction fingerprint/material, SecretAccessEvent and ActivityLog.
units.lifecycle: Listing returns only bound Agent plus run-manifest Project Secret metadata and emits no value-access event. Fetching a bound value returns key/value/version with no-store, first persists a redaction registration without embedding plaintext in the run snapshot, then records success. Concurrent identical registrations deduplicate. Persistence failure rejects delivery. Unbound values are denied. Low-trust review, task-bridge and skill-test callers cannot list or fetch.
units.testAssessment: Four strong database cases cover multiple binding layers, metadata-only listing, plaintext non-leak assertions, success audit, fail-closed redaction, concurrency deduplication and three restricted caller classes. Missing are cross-Company/run/Agent mismatches, revoked/rotated Secret versions, provider outage, lease/TTL/single-use delivery, response/body/log proxy leakage, memory zeroization, denial audit for unbound requests, purpose and data-export policy, high-risk approval, rate limiting, concurrent rotation, KMS/HSM and proof that redaction material itself is encrypted and access-controlled.
units.designRationale: Allow a running Agent to discover only assigned Secrets and fetch values when necessary, while registering exact redaction material before release so subsequent logs can be scrubbed and denying less trusted execution lanes entirely.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Secret delivery that is tenant-, Work-, Connector-, purpose- and data-policy-bound, keeps values out of the control-plane domain where possible and leaves a complete custody/access record.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT binding resolution, metadata/value separation, no-store, redaction-before-delivery, failure closure, run snapshot manifest and low-trust denial. Prefer execution-node injection or short-lived broker leases over plaintext control-plane API responses; bind every access to WorkExecution, ResponsibilityContract, purpose and export policy, use provider/version references, expiry and least-use scope, and audit allowed plus denied attempts without revealing Secret existence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A successful fetch is linked to Agent/run but not to an accountable human, exact permission/data contract or approval. Plaintext crosses the HTTP/control-plane boundary. An unbound Secret request is denied without a SecretAccessEvent or ActivityLog entry, leaving attempted access outside the responsibility record even if existence-hiding is desired.
